content.text:
Fixed. Here's what was wrong and what changed.

## Root cause

`lib/route.js:368` detected a duplicate-route insertion failure by string-matching the router's message against `` `Method '${opts.method}' already declared for route` ``. When `opts.method` is an array, template interpolation produces `Method 'GET,POST' already declared...`, but find-my-way names a single method (`Method 'GET' already declared for route '/' with constraints '{}'`). The match failed, so the raw find-my-way `Error` was rethrown with no `code`.

## Change — `lib/route.js:365-372`

```js
// the router names a single method in its error message, so when the
// route declares multiple methods we must look for any of them
const methods = Array.isArray(opts.method) ? opts.method : [opts.method]
const duplicatedMethod = methods.find(method => error.message.includes(`Method '${method}' already declared for route`))
if (duplicatedMethod !== undefined) {
  throw new FST_ERR_DUPLICATED_ROUTE(duplicatedMethod, opts.url)
}
```

The single-method path is unchanged in behavior; the array path now reports the *specific* duplicated method rather than the stringified array, so the message stays accurate (`Method 'GET' already declared for route '/'`). This also fixes `fastify.all()`, which passes `this.supportedMethods` — an array — and therefore had the same missing `code`.

Regression test added to `test/throw.test.js`, next to the existing single-method case, asserting both `error.code` and the message.

## COMPLEX.md compliance

- `lib/route.js` isn't itself ranked, but it co-changes with `fastify.js` (46%). **`fastify.js` did not need a change**: it only forwards `method` into `router.prepareRoute` (`fastify.js:178-202`, `:815`), and all duplicate-detection lives in `lib/route.js`. The `fastify.all` case is fixed entirely by the route-side change.
- **`lib/errors.js` was not touched** — `FST_ERR_DUPLICATED_ROUTE` already exists with the right message and arity — so **`docs/Reference/Errors.md` needed no change** either.
- Tests run green before and after: `test/throw.test.js`, `test/route.1-8`, `test/route-shorthand`, `test/route-prefix`, `test/constrained-routes`, `test/versioned-routes`, `test/internals/errors.test.js` — 245 pass, 0 fail.

Two caveats worth stating: the detection remains message-string-based, so it's still coupled to find-my-way's wording — an upstream message change would silently reintroduce this class of bug; and I could not run the linter (`npx eslint` needed approval that wasn't granted), though the added code follows the surrounding style. Nothing is committed.
